title: Demand signal smoothing & SKU concentration analysis — GPU procurement
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sheet for smoothing short-term demand signals from the hosted API and Dedicated clusters and translating them into a SKU-aware reorder pipeline. Goal is to reduce over-ordering noise, lower SKU concentration risk, and produce an actionable ordering cadence for the next 9–12 months.

Status / context:
- Draft: refining smoothing parameters and safety-day policy after last quarter’s spot shortages.
- Origin: follow-up to infra postmortem INFRA-3421 (capacity gap caused by a 3-week H100 lead-time variance).
- Audience: infra procurement, finance (capex), SRE on-call, and platform capacity owners.

Key definitions used in this sheet:
- Demand signal: 7-day rolling sum of GPU-hours consumed per region and per product (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Reorder window: the lead time + safety days (window used to trigger purchase planning).
- Safety-days: operating-days buffer expressed in days of average demand rather than a static % of inventory.
- SKU concentration index (Herfindahl-ish): sum of squared share of total active capacity by SKU; lower is more diversified.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Current active SKUs: H100-80GB (h100-80), A100-80GB (a100-80), L40-48GB (l40-48), T4-16GB (t4-16).
- Planning horizon: 12 months; monthly cadence for finance approvals, weekly cadence for ops signals.
- Lead times (baseline mean): h100-80=14 weeks, a100-80=8 weeks, l40-48=6 weeks, t4-16=3 weeks.
- Lead time volatility (std dev weeks): h100=2.8, a100=1.6, l40=1.2, t4=0.8 (derived from supplier SLAs and previous 18-month orders).
- Cost per unit (est): h100=USD 30k, a100=USD 10k, l40=USD 5.5k, t4=USD 1k.

Signal smoothing approach tried (notes):
1) Simple moving average (SMA) 14-day: reacts slowly, reduces false positives but under-reacts to real growth spikes (hosted api promotions).
2) Exponential smoothing (alpha=0.2): better for recent changes but creates jitter when usage is noisy.
3) Holt-Winters additive seasonality with 7-day period: overfitting weekly spikes (customer cron jobs).
4) Hybrid: EMA for short-term (7d alpha=0.35) combined with median-of-rolling-week to clip extreme spikes -> chosen as default for now.

Priority metric for reorder: probability that projected demand during reorder window exceeds projected capacity minus scheduled deliveries. We approximate by using the smoothed signal * reorder_window_days.

Example quick calc (region: us-west):
- Current deployed capacity: 320 H100-equivalent units (we map other SKUs to an "H100-eq" basis using performance weights: a100=0.33, l40=0.18, t4=0.03).
- 7d smoothed demand: 4,800 GPU-hours/day -> 33,600 GPU-hours/week.
- Reorder window for H100: 14w lead + 14 safetydays (~2w) => 16w => 112 days.
- Expected consumption in reorder window: 4,800 * 112 = 537,600 GPU-hours.
- H100 one-unit capacity (estimate for mapping): 24 GPU-hours/day (sustained) => 2,688 GPU-hours/112 days.
- Units needed (no buffer): 537,600 / 2,688 ≈ 200 H100-equivalent units.
- Apply safety-days policy (20 days equivalent): add 20 * 4,800 = 96,000 GPU-hours -> +36 units -> plan order ~236 H100-eq.

This example shows how long lead times amplify any smoothing errors. Our hybrid smoothing trimmed spike-driven orders by ~28% vs naive 7d raw-sum in backtest.

SKU concentration analysis (novel metric applied here):
- Compute concentration index C = sum_i (share_i)^2 where share_i is deployed capacity share by SKU.
- At the start of Q1, C(us-west)=0.63 (strongly H100-heavy). Target: reduce to <=0.45 by end of Q3.
- Strategy levers to reduce C: diversify small orders of faster-delivery SKUs (L40/T4) to meet near-term demand while staging H100 large orders for base capacity; negotiate split-shipment with supplier for partial early delivery.

Procurement pipeline design (staged):
- Weekly signal evaluation -> generate recommended order quantity per SKU per region.
- Monthly procurement round (finance approval): consolidate weekly recommendations into POs grouped by supplier and region to reduce transaction/transport overhead.
- Rolling 3-month firm plan + 9-month optional window (vendor option line) to keep flexibility.
- Exception path: emergency spot buy (cloud bursts) if projected shortfall probability > 25% and approval from SRE lead.

Order bundling heuristics (notes):
- Bundle by supplier family rather than SKU when possible to reduce lead-time variance. Historically, supplier X ships mixed A100/H100 batches with partial early shipments within 6–8w of order.
- For H100 specifically: use staggered tranches (30/40/30) across weeks 6/12/14 after order to smooth supply risk. Solicited in vendor negotiations.

Risk matrix (short-form):
- Long lead-time spikes (supplier delays): high likelihood; mitigation: increase safety-days by +25% for long-lead SKUs, maintain 10–15% cloud-spot reserve.
- SKU EOL / substitution risk: medium; maintain conversion mapping and procurement option lines for L40->A100 if vendor discontinues.
- Region-specific allocation disputes: low->medium; create per-region allocation priority list tied to SLA tiers (enterprise > dedicated > hosted).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Finance: acceptable capex cadence? Monthly POs vs quarterly POs (tradeoff: transaction costs vs agility).
- Procurement: from which suppliers can we request partial ship / staggered delivery contractually? (need legal review).
- SRE/product: acceptable safety-days by SLA tier (hosted API vs Dedicated customer clusters).

Backtest summary (past 12 months, simulated):
- Hybrid smoothing + safety-days policy: reduced unnecessary emergency cloud bursts by 62% and reduced peak reorder quantities by 28% vs naive 7d-sum triggers.
- Cost delta: Slightly higher near-term spend due to L40/T4 top-ups (~+3% capex) but lower spot-cloud opex (-12% over 12 months).

Operational runbook (short):
1) Every Monday: infra-signal job updates smoothed demand and publishes per-region SKU recommendations to /inventory-sim outputs (link in linked_artifacts).
2) On 1st of each month: procurement team consolidates weekly outputs into proposed POs; finance runs capital approval; default cadence: approve/adjust within 5 business days.
3) If shortfall probability > 25% (computed by monte-carlo sim with lead-time variance), trigger emergency review meeting (on-call, procurement, product).

Action items (owner & ETA):
- Finalize alpha for hybrid EMA (Ravi) — ETA: 2025-02-10.
- Negotiate partial-shipment clause for H100 with supplier-X (Marisol) — ETA: 2025-03-01.
- Add per-tenant SLA multiplier into safety-days calc (Ava) — ETA: 2025-02-20.
- Run 12-month sensitivity for 10%, 25%, 50% demand growth scenarios and commit results to finance (Jonah) — ETA: 2025-02-28.

Notes to self / scribbles:
- Consider switching safety-days from absolute days to a percentile of historical daily demand distribution for more robust tail behavior.
- Explore a small standing buffer of A100s in APAC to mitigate regional shipping chokepoints during lunar new year.
- Record of last emergency cloud burst: Jan 2024 — 46% H100 shortage over 3 weeks; led to two-week degraded latency for heavy-retry endpoints.

References / historical docs:
- INFRA-2710: Q4 2023 H100 shipment delay postmortem.
- Q3 2024: vendor pricing sheet (confidential) — vendor X offered 6% discount for 12+ month commit.

If you’re reviewing this as a stakeholder: comment inline, ping procurement for supplier contact info, and we’ll lock smoothing params next week.

-- end of draft sheet --
